title: Break The Spin · Breaking Nov 16
subtitle: Breaking: Iran dirty bomb intel. Top of Queue.

posts.theme: Iran dirty bomb plans for Washington (breaking)
posts.quote: U.S. INTEL: IRAN IS DRAWING UP PLANS FOR A DIRTY BOMB OR CHEMICAL ATTACK IN WASHINGTON. THE TARGETS: TOP TRUMP OFFICIALS.
posts.alt: Two panels: a photo of Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi seated behind an Iran nameplate on the left and a photo of the White House lit up at night on the right, with a red-ringed circle inset of a firefighter in a yellow hazmat suit sweeping for radiation during a training exercise. Bold text below reads: U.S. intel: Iran is drawing up plans for a dirty bomb or chemical attack in Washington. The targets: top Trump officials.
posts.caption:
U.S. intelligence indicates Iran is drawing up plans to hit senior Trump administration officials in Washington, D.C., with a dirty bomb or a chemical weapon, according to an exclusive CNN report citing seven U.S. officials.

Two of those sources said the planning is very specific, down to locations and targets. U.S. intelligence has also picked up Iranian chatter claiming bomb-making materials are already stashed inside the United States. Officials are split on how credible that claim is, but they broadly agree it would have been possible for Tehran to hide nuclear or chemical material here. One source pointed to the border: "it would have been extremely easy to get operatives inside the country."

The officials stress this is not an imminent attack. They describe Iran building options for itself. "Whether they actually have the personnel in place to execute is a matter of debate," one source said. Officials have held several meetings over the past week on how to respond.

A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive packed with radioactive material. Experts say most casualties would come from the blast itself, but the radiation could contaminate entire city blocks. "Any weapon like that is a weapon of terror, not a weapon of precision," one source said. "They can make people really sick and certain areas uninhabitable."

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said the administration is "monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland." Iran's UN mission rejected what it called "false and fabricated allegations" but did not directly address the dirty bomb intelligence. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence declined to comment.
posts.first:
Some context. The United States has been at war with Iran since February. American strikes and an economic blockade are squeezing the regime, and peace talks are stalled. Officials told CNN that if Iran's leaders came to fear for the regime's survival, they might decide the risk of retaliation is worth taking.

The threats are already changing how Washington lives. The Secret Service moved Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who runs the economic pressure campaign against Iran, onto a military base after Iranian threats against his life. Rubio, Hegseth and Stephen Miller have reportedly moved to protected housing too. Iran's answer to those reports came from Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi: "Worse than fake news is fake intelligence."

Tehran has done this before. In 2022 the Justice Department charged a member of Iran's Revolutionary Guard with plotting to murder former National Security Adviser John Bolton. In 2024 it charged an IRGC-tasked man in a plot to kill Donald Trump.

Meanwhile, a key spy tool has gone dark. The foreign surveillance authority known as Section 702 expired in June after a standoff between the White House and Congress. The Attorney General, the DNI and the CIA director have warned that the gap puts "the lives of both Americans in the homeland and our troops stationed abroad" at risk.

Critics on the left are already comparing this report to the Iraq WMD claims. Skepticism of anonymous sources is fair. But a regime that has spent years plotting to kill American officials on American soil has earned being taken seriously.
